scenarios.description: Drive a sequence of requests while capacity is available to expose normal admission flow and verify accepted responses preserve each request identifier.
Fill all tracking resources, then issue another request to expose capacity rejection behavior and verify overflow signaling.
Generate a valid response while keeping resp_ready low for several cycles to expose response holding behavior under backpressure.
Assert synchronous reset during an outstanding response and verify that the controller returns to an empty state without emitting the old response.
Issue repeated requests on consecutive cycles around the transition from full capacity to available capacity to expose resource accounting correctness.

requirements.description: A request is accepted only on a cycle where req_valid and req_ready are both high.
The controller must never allow queue_level to exceed MAX_ACTIVE.
An accepted request must eventually produce exactly one response containing the same req_id.
A rejected request caused by exhausted capacity must assert resp_accept low and set overflow high for that response.
The response identifier must remain stable while resp_valid is high and resp_ready is low.
The controller must support requests with all four req_class values and preserve the supplied req_id in the response.
queue_level must represent the number of accepted packets that have not completed their response handshake.
A request transfer occurs only when req_valid and req_ready are both high on the same rising clock edge.
req_id and req_class must be sampled only on a request transfer cycle; values outside a transfer cycle have no effect.
resp_valid may assert after a request transfer, and once asserted it must remain asserted until a cycle where resp_ready is high.
A response transfer occurs only when resp_valid and resp_ready are both high on the same rising clock edge.
resp_id and resp_accept must remain unchanged while resp_valid is high and resp_ready is low.
The controller must not accept a new request while it cannot preserve a pending response result.
The verification environment can demonstrate correct request and response handshake behavior.
The verification environment can demonstrate correct behavior at zero occupancy and maximum occupancy boundaries.
The verification environment can demonstrate that accepted requests are matched to exactly one response.
The verification environment can demonstrate that overflow reporting only occurs for capacity exhaustion.
The verification environment can demonstrate reset recovery from active transaction states.
